extraction.tier_rationale: Not a fitted ke0: the published quantity is the time to peak effect. Hypnos solves it on the Gepts kinetics to 0.1758/min; opentiva independently codes 0.17559 'calculated with TTPE of 5.6 min'.

23 surgical patients (14-68 y), arterial sampling to 48 h, three analysis methods. The authors found no relation of any parameter to age, weight or lean body mass, so the model is absolute. The PK values are quoted verbatim in the primary abstract. The PK parameters alone would be Tier B; the record is C because its ke0 is solved from a published time to peak effect, not fitted, and the worst input wins.
extraction.source_locator: Gepts 1995, Table 3 and abstract (log means, 95% CI)

source_review.reviewed_by: automated source cross-check (Claude Opus 5.5 via Hypnos)
source_review.method: compared each value to the primary-paper PubMed abstract (verbatim) and two open implementations; solved the ke0 independently
sources: https://github.com/StevenLShafer/stanpumpR (R/drugs_sufentanil.R: the printed Table 3 values; tPeak 5.6 min from Shafer & Varvel 1991, Fig 2)
https://github.com/opentiva/opentiva (opentiva/sufentanil.py, Gepts: V1 14.3, rate constants, ke0 0.17559 from TTPE 5.6 min)
source_review.notes: All six PK values and their 95% CIs match the abstract verbatim and stanpumpR exactly. opentiva's rate constants (k10 0.0645, k12 0.1086, k13 0.0229, k21 0.0245, k31 0.0014) agree to their printed rounding. Note: stanpumpR documents that back-calculating V3 from the rounded k31 gives 251.9 L, outside the paper's CI, so the printed volumes/clearances are curated, not rate constants. ke0: Hypnos solves 0.1758/min for a 5.6-min tpeak, against opentiva's 0.17559. HUMAN ITEMS: confirm Table 3, and confirm the 5.6-min tpeak in Shafer & Varvel 1991 Fig 2.

notes: Fentanyl family, second member. Context-sensitive like fentanyl but with a smaller late rise, which is the Shafer & Varvel 'rational opioid selection' point Hypnos can now show forward.
